title: What Are the Javanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Ranks US #1 for 'javanese wedding'. Publish method: update the existing page in place and change its slug; confirm a 301 from the old URL. Protect the ranking: keep covering every query the old page ranks for.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch; SEO pulls all its ranked keywords (US and AU) and the outline keeps covering them; meta title keeps 'Javanese wedding' near the front. Keep its traditions if sourceable; never reuse wording; drop errors; correct brand terms.

Overlap: /expert-advice/indonesian-wedding-traditions (draft) is the Indonesia overview and already covers siraman, midodareni, panggih and the akad from the Kraton Yogyakarta pages. This article goes deeper on Java only; the two link to each other. Reuse and re-check the Javanese facts in content/posts/indonesian-wedding-traditions/03-source-pack.json (fact_01 to fact_17) and the legal facts (fact_100+) before adding new sources.

Likely customs (brief finalises): nontoni and lamaran; peningsetan; pasang tarub and bleketepe; siraman; midodareni; ijab or akad in Muslim families; panggih (balangan gantal, wiji dadi egg-stepping, sindur binayang, kacar-kucur, dulangan); sungkeman; batik motifs such as sido mukti and truntum only where sourced; Solo and Yogyakarta styles (paes ageng); gamelan. UNESCO: Indonesian Batik (2009, text links it to marriage); Gamelan (2021) only if its text mentions weddings; no Wayang unless it does. Palace account framed as royal practice, never general practice.

Destination angle: marrying in Java or Bali, reusing the Indonesian article's Embassy-sourced legal facts after re-checking (same religion, CNI, 10 days' notice, KUA or Civil Registry, recognition in Australia) and Smartraveller's current Indonesia advice; Javanese-Australian weddings at home. Yogyakarta and Solo named only as places couples choose; no venue claims. 'As at November 2026'.

Sources: UNESCO, Kraton Yogyakarta and Kasunanan Surakarta official pages, Indonesian culture ministry pages, museums, academic journals. Unsourced becomes 'often told' with no meanings as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker. One honest framing line per section.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (batik cloth) labelled illustrative pending approval; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; no extra sourcing rounds.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.
Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or religious paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
